motivation: In 2008 Hideo Hosono discovered superconductivity at 26 K in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO. This opened the first new family of high-temperature superconductors since the cuprates, and it came from iron, an element long thought hostile to superconductivity. Within weeks, Xianhui Chen and Zhongxian Zhao showed that rare-earth substitution raises Tc above 40 K and then to 55 K. This established a genuine second class of unconventional high-Tc superconductors. The iron pnictides and chalcogenides are intrinsically multiband: several Fermi-surface pockets carry distinct gaps, probably with sign-changing s± pairing mediated by spin fluctuations. That has turned multicomponent superconductivity from a theoretical curiosity into an experimental reality, with nematicity, time-reversal-symmetry breaking states, topological surface Majorana modes in Fe(Te,Se), and technologically relevant high-field wires and films. The discovery reshaped our understanding of unconventional pairing, and nearly two decades of work have confirmed its lasting importance.
